thread:
tara: Heads-up — we've been getting a surge of RBAC audit alerts this morning around `role_grant` for the `infra-automation` principal. Spamming the alerts channel.
oleg: Yup saw it. Lots of `audit.log` entries saying `role_grant` + `target: service_account` between 06:00-06:12. Most correlate to scheduled infra job runs.
maria: That infra-automation principal is our CI/CD runner that applies TF changes. It's expected to touch roles during canary deploys, but the volume is drowning real signals.
alex: Screenshot of SIEM counts? can we pivot to the dashboard? :chart_with_upwards_trend:
sec-bot: Alert: "RBAC change - suspicious grant" triggered 87 times in 12m for principal=infra-automation. Rule: `event.action:role_grant AND severity>=medium AND NOT trusted_principal:true`.
tara: Dumping a quick query we used: ```kql
index=audit event.action=role_grant | stats count by principal, target, result | sort -count
``` 
oleg: Proposal: add an enrichment check for known automation principals and either suppress or noise-score them. Options:
- add `AND NOT principal:infra-automation` to the rule (fast but hard-coded)
- add a suppression window per principal (e.g., 10 alerts per 5m suppressed)
- add context enrichment: if event has `ci_job_id` or `git.commit` then lower priority
maria: +1 for suppression window and enrichment. We cannot whitelist completely because infra-automation sometimes legitimately fails and should still alert at high severity.
alex: What about putting a small ML dedupe on identical `target`+`change` within 1m? That would cut noise for repetitive idempotent ops.
sec-bot: Suggestion recorded: create a new signal level `noise` for advisory hits. Also recommend tagging existing alerts with `automation=true` when `user_agent` contains `gitlab-runner` or `infra-automation`.
tara: Two action items: 1) Add enrichment rules to parse `ci_job_id` and `user_agent`, 2) Change detection to a rate-based suppression: 10 events / 5m per principal -> escalate on 11th. Who owns?
oleg: I'll take 1) enrichment parsing. I'll add fields: `automation_principal`, `ci_job`, and `commit_sha` to the normalized doc. ETA today.
maria: I'll draft the suppression rule in SIEM. Draft logic: ```sql
WHEN count(event_id) BY principal,rule_id WITHIN 5m > 10
  THEN suppress AND create summary_alert(count, samples)
``` 
alex: Can we also add a dashboard widget that shows top noisy principals and a toggle to view suppressed alerts? Helps audits and postmortem.
tara: Yes please. Also we need an audit trail so suppression isn't invisible. Any suppressed batch should create a low-noise summary event with samples and link to raw logs.
sec-bot: Note: suppression summary will be auto-tagged `suppressed:true` and `suppress_reason:rate_limit`.
oleg: I'll push enrichment PR and link to the SIEM PR after CI passes. Will include test logs.
maria: I'll handle the SIEM rule change and add unit tests in the detection repo. Will cc security@redwood on the PR.
alex: Quick check — do we need a temporary playbook update for oncall? I can add a line: "If suppressed summary count > 100 in 1h escalate to pager".
tara: Good idea. Add that to the oncall playbook and notify infra team so they can reduce churn if needed.
oleg: Sending PRs now. Will post links when ready.
maria: PR for suppression posted: https://git.internal/rules/123 (draft). Includes tests + dashboard draft.
tara: Great work — let's monitor for 24h and regroup. If suppression misses a real signal, revert and iterate. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Incident note appended: "RBAC audit noise from infra-automation — tuned suppression + enrichment applied (monitoring)".
